enabled.description: Register the action batcher with the egress mediator. Its enforce/audit/off mode is the mediator's stages["egress-action-batcher"] entry (default: enforce).

windowMs.description: Batching window (default 250 ms; an integer from 250 to 10000, anything else is refused). Capacity: only actions that fall in the same window are reordered or collapsed, so a longer window covers more of a burst. Cost: up to windowMs added latency per batched tool call.

canonicalOrder.description: Release a window's independent actions sorted by SHA-256 of their canonical encoding (always on: false is refused). Capacity: removes the sequence channel (for k actions from N, k*log2(N) bits fall to the multiset bound log2(C(N+k-1,k))). Cost: the window's buffering latency; dependent actions keep their order.

collapseIdempotentRepeats.description: Collapse repeats of idempotent actions (always on: false is refused), keyed on the request actually sent (no fragment, no bare '?'): GET/HEAD/OPTIONS within the window and, for the rest of the run, from the recorded outcome of the one request that left (errors included); PUT/DELETE and identical file writes within the window only, and only when no other side-effecting action on the same resource shares the window. POST, messages, sends and unknown actions are never collapsed. Capacity: removes the count channel (multiset bound falls to the subset bound, N bits). Cost: a repeat gets the identical call's recorded result (reproduced exactly through the host's tool replay seam) instead of being re-sent. Within one run, a repeated read may be answered from a recent copy.

cacheTtlMs.description: Cross-window answering of side-effect-free repeats (default 30000; an integer from 1 to 600000, 0 is refused). It is on for the run's whole lifetime; within one run, a repeated read may be answered from a recent copy. A record is cleared only by an action that may change what it reads: an unsafe-method HTTP request to its origin, or a side-effecting tool call or send that names its origin. When memory budgets drop a record, its repeat is refused, never re-sent.

padding.description: Constant-set padding (default off). Each active window issues every member of allowedSet that the agent did not choose, as a dummy request through the padded tool's own request path (web_fetch: same headers, SSRF guard, byte limit and cancel, error-body limit and provider fallback), in lockstep with the real requests, on a fixed window grid. Fail-closed: with no request client the window is blocked. A request outside allowedSet leaks its identity: 9 bits per wire byte plus 1 are charged to the capacity ledger before release; the window holds up to 10 s for the ledger, then refuses that request. Capacity: the observed set is constant, so the per-window choice capacity is 0 for actions inside allowedSet. Cost: |allowedSet| requests per active window, plus grid-alignment latency. Requires collapseIdempotentRepeats to also hide counts.

allowedSet.description: Actions to keep constant: a URL string (GET) or { method, url } with method GET, HEAD or OPTIONS. Any other entry is refused; with padding enabled the set must not be empty.

tools.description: Tool names in scope at the tool-call chokepoint; the defaults can only be added to (default: message, sessions_send, web_fetch, web_search, x_search, browser, write; shell tools when their command reaches the network). A tool in scope is batched only through a declared mapping from its call to the request it sends (web_fetch: a GET of its URL; write: the file it writes), never on its parameters; one without a mapping is refused while the stage enforces, with an unmapped-tool audit record.
